one-check-per-line.why: all 4 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 4

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 4 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why: The criterion holds. I compared each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against the words of its expect line. Check 1 tests that padLeft is exported, pads on the left, uses fill or a space when fill is left out, and reaches width ("00042", "  ab", "**x"). Those are just cases the words already demand. Check 2 needs '"abc" "abcdef" "abcdef"' to come back unchanged, which is exactly what the line says. Check 3 asks for "a heading that names it with text about it" for every exported function. That is a fair reading of "section", and it does not require any heading format. Check 4 passes when npm test "exits 0 with no failing tests". The stricter items all sit under "Advisory (not PASS/FAIL conditions)": whether the tests cover padLeft, whether headings follow the `## name(args)` style, and whether the other functions behave as before. None of the checks requires mutation tests, a branch or file scope, or exact wording.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs. The builder only runs `npm test`, and package.json defines it as `node --test`. The verifier runs three `node --input-type=module -e "..."` one-liners plus `npm test`. All three import './index.js' from the repo root, and that file is tracked. The shell quoting is valid: the outer double quotes contain only single-quoted JS strings, with no `$`, backticks or `!` that the shell would expand. The JS is valid ESM. For example, `Object.entries(m).filter(([,v])=>typeof v==='function').map(([k])=>k).join(' ')` parses, and the named import `{padLeft}` resolves once step 1 adds the export. `--input-type=module` with `-e` is a valid combination of node flags. Even if index.js were CommonJS, a dynamic ESM import of it would still work through interop. No command names a missing file, script or tool.

catches-traps.why:
I checked the output against all three must_catch items, and each one is handled.
1. Builder step 2 adds a slugify section along with padLeft: "Also add the missing `## slugify(s)` section…". The "Current state" part also says slugify has no section, so line 3 already fails before the change.
2. Verifier Check 3 lists the exported functions at the PR head and requires a section for each one, "at least capitalize, slugify, truncate and padLeft". It FAILs if "any exported function has no section" and points to slugify by name.
3. Verifier Check 1 calls `padLeft('ab',4)` without a fill argument and expects "  ab" (two spaces, then ab). It FAILs on "no space when fill is left out".
No part of the output breaks the criterion.

avoids-must-not.why: The briefs avoid both must_not items. Item 1: verifier Check 3 can't pass when slugify has no section. It lists every exported function, says "every function in that list (at least capitalize, slugify, truncate and padLeft) has its own section", and adds "the base README has no slugify section, so look for that one in particular." Item 2: no PASS/FAIL condition is stricter than its line. Check 1 tests exact outputs that follow from the line, and it does not require a one-character fill or check the parameter count. Check 3 defines a section only as "a heading that names it with text about it", not a required layout. The `## name(args)` style, test coverage and how the other functions behave appear only under "Advisory (not PASS/FAIL conditions)". The builder brief suggests a heading format, but it sets no PASS/FAIL condition, so it doesn't break the rule.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief's checks. The builder brief repeats the verifier's probe inputs and their expected outputs. In Step 1 it gives "padLeft('42', 5, '0') === '00042' and padLeft('ab', 4) === '  ab'", and Step 3 repeats "('42', 5 -> '00042')". Verifier Check 1 calls exactly padLeft('42',5,'0') and padLeft('ab',4) and needs "00042" and "  ab" to pass. Step 3 also lists the same cases as Check 2: s exactly width long and s longer than width, both unchanged. So the builder gets part of the checker's input/expected-output set, which the criterion forbids. Telling the builder to run npm test and to write tests is allowed. The overlapping concrete probes are not.
